answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. Reputation and voting weight accrue to that locked stake over time, while proven fraud burns part of it and can exclude the identity from future work. Creating a thousand aliases does not multiply influence without also locking a thousand stakes, so a sybil attack becomes costly in capital and foregone liquidity. A juniper, timber, or ocean-themed account name grants no extra weight: only bonded resources do.
